item.title: A Linear-Time Algorithm for the Unbiased Claw Game on Graphs with Maximum Degree 4
item.description: arXiv:2610.21878v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the unbiased Maker-Breaker $K_{1,3}$-game, the unbiased claw game, played on the edge set of a general graph $G$. In this game, Maker and Breaker alternatingly claim edges of $G$, and Maker wins if his claimed edges contain a claw once no more edges are available. Graphs with maximum degree at least 5 are Maker's win. A graph $G$ is claw-connected if the hypergraph modeling the unbiased claw game played on $G$ is connected. We characterize Maker's win in the unbiased claw game on every claw-connected graph whose maximum degree is different from 3. Our main structural result is a complete characterization of Maker's win for claw-connected graphs with exactly one vertex of degree 4. The analysis is based on the fact that vertices of degree 4 act as forcing structures. Our characterization results in a linear-time algorithm for the unbiased claw game on claw-connected graphs with maximum degree different from 3. We also obtain a linear-time decomposition algorithm reducing the game on general graphs to a collection of pairwise edge-disjoint claw-connected subgraphs of maximum degree exactly 3, thereby isolating the only remaining case. This decomposition yields an $\mathcal{O}(|V(G)|^3)$-time algorithm for the unbiased claw game on general graphs, improving on the $\mathcal{O}(|V(G)|^7)$-time algorithm implied by the work of Galliot, Gravier and Sivignon (arXiv 2026). For a lower bound on the decision complexity, we prove that any agent deciding the game in the adjacency-array model makes at least $\Omega(|V(G)|)$ queries in the worst case, indicating the optimality of our linear-time algorithm.
item.dc:creator: Julian Christoph Brinkmann

item.title: Automating Observable Closure Analysis for Graph Transformation Models with MolFoundry
item.description: arXiv:2610.20821v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Graph transformations model changing systems, with applications in software, biology and chemistry, among others. We introduce MolFoundry, a graph transformation framework, and present a workflow for observable analysis that tracks the dynamics of local patterns through rule composition. Analysing rule compositions avoids the need to enumerate a potentially infinite state space. Building on rule-algebraic stochastic rewriting, MolFoundry's kernel composes rules with nested application conditions, including missing-edge constraints. Given rules, rates and query patterns, the algorithms iteratively identify auxiliary pattern counts and search for closure. Using exact counting identities supplied by graph-family backends, successful searches yield closed ordinary differential equations for average counts or, with justified individual jumps, finite event models describing joint changes and rates. We evaluate conditional composition and automated discovery of auxiliary observables against published calculations and independent rule application. Applications to aldol addition, copolymerization and chlorination show how the framework yields quantitative predictions directly from molecular graph rules.
item.dc:creator: Marcel Friedrichs, Addie Jordon, Juri Kol\v{c}\'{a}k, Daniel Merkle

item.title: The Koml\'os Problem in Matrix-Multiplication Time
item.description: arXiv:2610.20995v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a randomized algorithm that, for an $m\times n$ matrix whose columns have Euclidean norm at most one, finds a signing with discrepancy below $99$ in expected $\widetilde O(L_{\mathrm{in}}+n^\omega)$ bit operations, where $L_{\mathrm{in}}$ is the input encoding length and $\omega$ is the exponent of matrix multiplication. The previous fastest algorithm with a constant discrepancy bound, due to Li, is deterministic and uses $O(mn+n^{\omega+2}\log^3 n)$ arithmetic operations. We build on the spectral signing framework of Guo, Fang, and Lu and of Li, which rounds a single fractional coloring while one spectral potential controls every row. Li's potential tracks a top eigenvalue, and the gap below that eigenvalue, which can be of order $1/n$, limits the length of every step. We replace it with a resolvent potential that is smooth without any gap condition, and we draw step signs at random, so that the potential only needs to be concave while progress is measured separately. Our key insight is to reuse a single subspace of directions throughout a batch of steps, thereby using only one spectral computation, so that the more expensive linear algebraic operations are paid for only polylogarithmically often at each scale. Within a batch, we sample directions from a Gaussian completion matrix whose inverse we maintain under rank-one row replacements. Finally, we use a finite-precision analysis to prove stability of the algorithm and attain the bit-complexity bound.
item.dc:creator: Emile Anand, Peter Chen

item.title: Metric Dimension is NP-complete on Graphs of Treewidth Two
item.description: arXiv:2610.21133v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The metric dimension of a connected graph is the least number of vertices whose distance vectors distinguish all vertices. We show that deciding whether the metric dimension of a graph is at most a given integer is NP-complete on graphs of treewidth at most two. As the problem is polynomial on trees, the graphs of treewidth one, this settles the treewidth threshold of its hardness, which was known to lie between two and twenty-four. The reduction is from satisfiability of formulas in which every literal occurs at most twice. To such a formula with $n$ clauses and $r$ variables it associates a graph $G_\varphi$ of treewidth at most two with $O((n+r)^2)$ vertices, whose metric dimension is $2(n+r)+5$ if the formula is satisfiable and $2(n+r)+6$ otherwise.
item.dc:creator: Tristan Benoit

item.title: Barrier Log-Concavity of Large Forests
item.description: arXiv:2610.22098v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the independence sequence of every sufficiently large forest is strictly barrier log-concave: whenever $i_{k+1}>i_k$, one has $i_k^2>i_{k-1}i_{k+1}$. Consequently, every common downward coefficient tilt is unimodal, with one order threshold valid simultaneously for all $0<t\le1$. As an application, we prove that every sufficiently large well-covered tree has a strictly log-concave independence polynomial. More generally, the latter conclusion holds for well-covered forests with sufficiently large matching number. Every sufficiently large forest with a palindromic independence polynomial is also strictly log-concave, with its modes at the central ranks. The proof establishes local coefficient-curvature estimates uniformly over forests of unbounded maximum degree and over activities tending to zero. Combined with the fixed-density theorem of Fang, Lu, Nevo, Yao, and Zheng, these estimates complete the strict log-concavity interval down to rank one through $\lfloor17\alpha/25\rfloor$; the terminal fraction is inherited. The classical decreasing tail then yields the barrier property. A cumulative-coefficient corona theorem transfers barrier log-concavity of the base forest to full strict log-concavity of its leaf corona.
item.dc:creator: Vadim E. Levit

item.title: Connectivity Bounds for GHZ Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.22190v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) states are multipartite entangled quantum states that play a central role in quantum information theory, with applications in quantum communication, cryptography, and distributed quantum computing. A major experimental goal is to create high-dimensional GHZ states using multiple entangled parties. Krenn, Gu and Zeilinger discovered a surprising bridge between these quantum-optical experiments and graph theory: certain photonic experiments can be represented by edge-coloured, edge-weighted graphs, and the dimension of the produced GHZ state equals the number of feasible monochromatic inherited vertex colourings. This led Krenn and Gu to conjecture that every GHZ graph with more than four vertices has dimension at most $2$. A counterexample would give a new high-dimensional multipartite GHZ construction, while a proof would clarify fundamental resource limitations in quantum optics. It is known that the conjecture holds for graphs of vertex connectivity at most $2$ [MFCS 2024], and that simple GHZ graphs with $n>4$ vertices have dimension less than $n/\sqrt{2}$ [Quantum 2024]. However, no general upper bound depending only on vertex connectivity was known. We prove that every simple connected GHZ graph $G$ with at least four vertices has dimension at most $2^{\kappa(G)-1}+\binom{\kappa(G)}{2}$, where $\kappa(G)$ is the vertex connectivity of $G$. We also prove new bounds in terms of edge connectivity and maximum degree.
item.dc:creator: L. Sunil Chandran, Rishikesh Gajjala

item.title: Geometric Graph Representations via Compact SAT Encodings
item.description: arXiv:2610.22241v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present compact SAT encodings and certifying exact solvers for boxicity and cubicity. The boxicity of a graph is the minimum dimension in which it is the intersection graph of axis-aligned boxes; cubicity is defined analogously using unit cubes. Grid-based formulations face a geometric discretization bottleneck, growing rapidly with the target dimension. We avoid this bottleneck by encoding the total order of interval endpoints in each coordinate. For an $n$-vertex graph and target dimension $d$, our boxicity encoding uses $O(n^2d)$ variables and $O(n^3d)$ clauses, both linear in $d$. Requiring the left- and right-endpoint orders to agree yields a cubicity encoding of the same asymptotic size. Satisfying models are decoded into independently checked geometric representations, while unsatisfiable instances used as lower-bound evidence carry mechanically verified DRAT certificates. In a controlled evaluation with 186 trials per encoding on standard and structured graph families, the order encoding solves 96.8% of trials, compared with 71.0% for the known grid formulation, and reduces mean PAR-2 time from 178.21 to 21.70 seconds. The pipeline also certifies exact values for several named graphs. We turn one such value into a reusable obstruction by proving that every Kneser graph $K(n,k)$ with $k\ge3$ and $n\ge2k+1$ contains an induced Desargues graph. The resulting lower bound, together with an explicit three-dimensional representation of $K(7,3)$, establishes $\operatorname{boxicity}(K(7,3))=3$. This disproves the conjecture of Caoduro and Sebo that $\operatorname{boxicity}(K(n,k))=n-k$ for all $k\ge3$ and $n\ge2k+1$.
item.dc:creator: L. Sunil Chandran, Rishikesh Gajjala, Suraj Kumar Sahoo, Aatman Supkar

item.title: Ternary Binomial and Trinomial Bent Functions in the Completed Maiorana-McFarland Class
item.description: arXiv:2507.20715v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Two classes of ternary (vectorial) bent functions of degree four with two and three terms in the univariate representation that belong to the completed Maiorana-McFarland original class are found. Binomials are mappings $\F_{3^{4k}}\mapsto\fthreek$ given by $\Tr^{4k}_k\big(a_1 x^{2(3^k+1)}+a_2 x^{(3^k+1)^2}\big)$, where $a_1$ is a nonsquare in $\F_{3^{4k}}$ and $a_2$ is defined explicitly by $a_1$. Particular subclass of such binomial vectorial bent function is represented by the exceptional polynomials over $\fthreek$. Bent trinomials are mappings $\F_{3^{2k}}\mapsto\fthree$ given by $\Tr_{2k}\big(a_1 x^{2(3^k+2)} + a_2 x^{3^k+5} + a_3 x^2\big)$ with $k>1$ not divisible by four and coefficients explicitly defined depending on the parity of $k$. The proof is based on new criterion that allows checking bentness by analyzing the first-order derivatives of $f$ in the direction of a chosen $n/2$-dimensional subspace ($n$ is the degree of the domain of $f$ over $\fp$).
item.dc:creator: Tor Helleseth, Alexander Kholosha, Niki Spithaki

item.title: Minimizing the makespan in job shop scheduling under conflict graph constraints
item.description: arXiv:2609.04161v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the job shop scheduling problem with a conflict graph, in which adjacent jobs cannot be processed simultaneously on different machines, with the objective of minimizing the makespan. We establish a polynomial equivalence with a resource-constrained job shop problem having unit-capacity resources and binary resource requirements The problem is strongly NP-hard even on two machines with unit-time operations. For this setting, we derive an optimal-makespan formula and a linear-time algorithm when the conflict graph is a cluster graph, given the clique partition. We also develop a polynomial-time $4/3$-approximation algorithm for arbitrary conflict graphs on two machines when each job has exactly two unit-time operations. For the general problem, we propose four mixed-integer linear formulations, lower bounds, and a genetic algorithm with active, non-delay, and hybrid decoding procedures. Computational experiments on instances derived from the Lawrence and Taillard benchmarks and on randomly generated generalized job shop instances evaluate the proposed methods and show that the genetic algorithm generally improves on constructive heuristics.
item.dc:creator: Nour Elhouda Tellache, Abdenour Azerine

item.title: Reweighted Spectral Partitioning Works: A Simple Algorithm for Vertex Separators in Special Graph Classes
item.description: arXiv:2506.01228v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish that a practical polynomial-time algorithm obtains near-optimal $\frac23$-balanced vertex separators for a number of graph classes, including genus-$g$ graphs, $K_h$-minor-free graphs, and geometric graphs. For many of these classes, our polynomial-time separator bounds improve on previous work. Moreover, unlike previous work, all these separators are produced by a single unified algorithm that has no specialization for the graph class, and this algorithm admits a scalable implementation with good empirical results. Furthermore, our approach is robust to graphs falling just outside these classes, making it appropriate for practical applications like road networks. A key distinction of our approach, compared to previous work, is the disentanglement of our algorithm and its analysis for specific graph classes. Our algorithm is based on a newly improved form of a recent Cheeger-style inequality relating the value of a special semidefinite program to vertex expansion. Our analysis then only has to directly bound the value of this semidefinite program for each graph class, and constructions for these bounds need not be algorithmic. Finally, we obtain several results of independent interest. These include an improved (existential) separator theorem for intersection graphs of $k$-ply $d$-dimensional balls, an improved bound on the Fiedler value of genus-$g$ graphs, and a complete spectral proof of the planar separator theorem.
item.dc:creator: Jack Spalding-Jamieson

item.title: Burling graphs in graphs with large chromatic number
item.description: arXiv:2510.19650v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A graph class is $\chi$-bounded if the only way to force large chromatic number in graphs from the class is by forming a large clique. In the 1970s, Erd\H{o}s conjectured that intersection graphs of straight-line segments in the plane are $\chi$-bounded, but this was disproved by Pawlik et al. (2014), who showed another way to force large chromatic number in this class -- by triangle-free graphs $B_k$ with $\chi(B_k)=k$ constructed by Burling (1965). This also disproved the celebrated conjecture of Scott (1997) that classes of graphs excluding induced subdivisions of a fixed graph are $\chi$-bounded. We prove that in broad classes of graphs excluding induced subdivisions of a fixed graph, including the increasingly more general classes of segment intersection graphs, string graphs, region intersection graphs, and hereditary classes of graphs with finite asymptotic dimension, large chromatic number can be forced only by large cliques or large graphs $B_k$. One corollary is that the hereditary closure of $\{B_k\colon k\geq 1\}$ forms a minimal hereditary graph class with unbounded chromatic number -- the second known graph class with this property after the class of complete graphs. Another corollary is that the decision variant of approximate coloring in the aforementioned graph classes can be solved in polynomial time by exhaustively searching for a sufficiently large clique or copy of $B_k$. We also discuss how our results along with some results of Chudnovsky, Scott, and Seymour on the existence of colorings can be turned into polynomial-time algorithms for the search variant of approximate coloring in string graphs (with intersection model in the input) and other aforementioned graph classes. Such an algorithm has not yet been known for any graph class that is not $\chi$-bounded.
item.dc:creator: Tara Abrishami, Marcin Bria\'nski, James Davies, Xiying Du, Jana Masa\v{r}\'ikov\'a, Pawe{\l} Rz\k{a}\.zewski, Bartosz Walczak

item.title: Arithmetic Circuits and Neural Networks for Regular Matroids
item.description: arXiv:2511.02406v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that there exist uniform $(+,\times,/)$-circuits of size $O(n^3)$ to compute the basis generating polynomial of regular matroids on $n$ elements. By tropicalization, this implies that there exist uniform $(\max,+,-)$-circuits and ReLU neural networks of the same size for weighted basis maximization of regular matroids. As a consequence in linear programming theory, we obtain a first example where taking the difference of two extended formulations can be more efficient than the best known individual extended formulation for the base polytope of regular matroids of size $O(n^6)$ by Aprile and Fiorini. Such differences have recently been introduced as virtual extended formulations. The proof of our main result relies on a fine-tuned version of Seymour's decomposition of regular matroids which allows us to identify and maintain graphic substructures to which we can apply a local version of the star-mesh transformation.
item.dc:creator: Christoph Hertrich, Stefan Kober, Georg Loho

item.title: Empirical Quantum Advantage in Constrained Optimization from Encoded Unitary Designs
item.description: arXiv:2511.14296v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce the Constraint-Enhanced Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (CE-QAOA), a shallow, constraint-aware ansatz that operates inside the one-hot product space [n]^m, where m is the number of blocks and each block is initialized in an n-qubit W_n state. We give an ancilla-free, depth-optimal encoder that prepares W_n using n-1 two-qubit rotations per block, and a two-local block-XY mixer that preserves the one-hot manifold and has a constant spectral gap on the one-excitation sector. At the level of expressivity, we establish per-block controllability, implying approximate universality per block. At the level of distributional behavior, we show that, after natural block and symbol permutation twirls, shallow CE-QAOA realizes an encoded unitary 1-design and supports approximate second-moment (2-design) behavior; combined with a Paley-Zygmund argument, this yields finite-shot anticoncentration guarantees. Algorithmically, we wrap constant-depth sampling with a deterministic feasibility checker to obtain a polynomial-time hybrid quantum-classical solver (PHQC) that returns the best observed feasible solution in O(S n^2) time, where S is a polynomial shot budget. We obtain two advantages. First, when CE-QAOA fixes r >= 1 locations different from the start city, we achieve a Theta(n^r) reduction in shot complexity even against a classical sampler that draws uniformly from the feasible set. Second, against a classical baseline restricted to raw bitstring sampling, we show an exp(Theta(n^2)) minimax separation. In noiseless circuit simulations of traveling salesman problem instances with n in {4,...,10} locations from the QOPTLib benchmark library, we recover the global optimum at depth p = 1 using polynomial shot budgets and coarse parameter grids defined by the problem size.
item.dc:creator: Chinonso Onah, Roman Firt, Kristel Michielsen

item.title: Computing bounded solutions to linear Diophantine equations with the sum of divisors
item.description: arXiv:2601.17832v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose an efficient computational method for finding all solutions $n\leq U$ to the Diophantine equation $a\sigma(n)=bn+c$, where $a,b,c$ are fixed integer coefficients, $U$ is a given upper bound, and $\sigma(n)$ denotes the sum of divisors of $n$. The method combines advanced pruning of possible prime factors of $n$ and their combinations with several optimization techniques, organized around a \emph{prime-wheel} data structure developed for this purpose. It is implemented in the {\sc SageMath} computer algebra system within the framework of recursively enumerated sets and supports native {\sc MapReduce} parallelization. We apply the method to numerous previously studied equations, discovering new solutions, certifying complete solution lists below substantially larger bounds than previously reported, and substantially improving lower bounds in several open problems involving the sum-of-divisors function.
item.dc:creator: Max A. Alekseyev

item.title: Investigating mixed-integer programming approaches for the $p$-$\alpha$-closest-center problem
item.description: arXiv:2603.13214v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work, we introduce and study the $p$-$\alpha$-closest-center problem ($p\alpha$CCP), which generalizes the $p$-second-center problem, a recently emerged variant of the classical $p$-center problem. In the $p\alpha$CCP, we are given sets of customers and potential facility locations, distances between each customer and potential facility location as well as two integers $p$ and $\alpha$. The goal is to open facilities at $p$ of the potential facility locations, such that the maximum $\alpha$-distance between each customer and the open facilities is minimized. The $\alpha$-distance of a customer is defined as the sum of distances from the customer to its $\alpha$ closest open facilities. If $\alpha$ is one, the $p\alpha$CCP is the $p$-center problem, and for $\alpha$ being two, the $p$-second-center problem is obtained, for which the only existing algorithm in literature is a variable neighborhood search (VNS). We present four mixed-integer programming (MIP) formulations for the $p\alpha$CCP, strengthen them by adding valid and optimality-preserving inequalities and conduct a polyhedral study to prove relationships between their linear programming relaxations. Moreover, we present iterative procedures for lifting some valid inequalities to improve initial lower bounds on the optimal objective function value of the $p\alpha$CCP and characterize the best lower bounds obtainable by this iterative lifting approach. Based on our theoretical findings, we develop a branch-and-cut algorithm (B&C) to solve the $p\alpha$CCP exactly. We improve its performance by a starting and a primal heuristic, variable fixings and separating inequalities. In our computational study, we investigate the effect of the various ingredients of our B&C on benchmark instances from related literature. Our B&C is able to prove optimality for 17 of the 40 instances from the work on the VNS heuristic.
item.dc:creator: Elisabeth Gaar, Sara Joosten, Markus Sinnl

item.title: Efficient sampling of the unlabeled structure of uniform random mappings and surjections
item.description: arXiv:2605.24068v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This article deals with the sampling and statistics of uniform random mappings and surjections from $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ to $[k]=\{1,\ldots,k\}$. More precisely, we focus on statistics that are invariant under relabeling of the domain and codomain. The structure of a mapping or surjection up to relabeling is captured by a compact representation called its profile. The profile records, for each occurring preimage size, the number of preimages of that size. We provide a complete set of algorithms that directly sample the profiles of uniform random mappings and surjections, covering the full parameter space. Their expected running times match the expected length of their outputs up to logarithmic factors. It is important to note that we make no assumption about the relationship between $n$ and $k$; in particular, we do not assume that $n/k$ is constant. All our guarantees are uniform in $n$ and $k$. Achieving this uniformity substantially complicates the analysis. Our algorithms are based on exact-size Boltzmann samplers, which we accelerate by optimizing the cost of each sampling round and increasing the acceptance probability. As spin-off results, we answer, up to a logarithmic factor, an open question of Devroye and Los~25 on sampling profiles of random mappings when $n>k\log k$, and obtain a sampler for uniform random surjections with expected running time $O(n\log k)$, valid across the full parameter space.
item.dc:creator: Arnaud Carayol, Pablo Rotondo

item.title: On balanced subfamilies of maximum complement-free families in the middle layer of the Boolean lattice
item.description: arXiv:2606.16172v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study balanced subfamilies of the middle layer $\binom{[2n]}{n}$ of the Boolean lattice $2^{[2n]}$. A family $\mathcal{F}\subseteq\binom{[2n]}{n}$ is said to be balanced if every element in $[2n]$ appears in the same number of members of $\mathcal{F}$. A balanced subfamily of size 2 is exactly a complementary pair $\{A,[2n]\setminus A\}$, and therefore a family with no balanced subfamily of size $2$ has at most $\frac{1}{2}\binom{2n}{n}$ members. We show that for every $k\geq 1$ and all sufficiently large $n$, this maximum size is compatible with delaying the smallest size of a balanced subfamily until $2k+2$. More precisely, there exists a family $\mathcal{F}\subseteq\binom{[2n]}{n}$ of size $\frac{1}{2}\binom{2n}{n}$ with no balanced subfamilies of sizes $2,4,\ldots,2k$, but with a balanced subfamily of size $2k+2$. The proof is constructive and uses a general lifting from simple games to self-dual selectors in the middle layer. This provides an efficient constructive proof of a recent conjecture of Moss and Pedersen.
item.dc:creator: Sa'ul A. Blanco

item.title: Optimal Unambiguous DNFs and Alon-Saks-Seymour
item.description: arXiv:2608.02533v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct unambiguous DNFs having width $O(n)$ but $0$-certificate complexity $\Omega(n^2)$. By utilizing the special structure of these DNFs, we prove a lifting theorem with a constant-sized gadget that lifts the DNF to a communication problem, while losslessly translating the separation in certificate complexity to a separation in communication complexity. This leads to an optimal refutation of the Alon-Saks-Seymour conjecture, as well as an optimal communication lower bound for the Clique versus Independent Set problem, improving the previous results of Balodis, Ben-David, G\"{o}\"{o}s, Jain and Kothari (FOCS 2021, SICOMP 2023) by several doubly logarithmic factors. As further applications of our construction to query complexity and learning theory, we exhibit: (a) a family of Boolean functions that has an optimal quartic separation between certificate complexity and approximate degree, and (b) a sample compression lower bound of $\Omega(\sqrt{\log c})$ for multiclass concept classes over $c$ labels.
item.dc:creator: Chirag Pabbaraju

item.title: There is no $8$-regular $K_3$-irregular graph
item.description: arXiv:2609.37978v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A graph is $K_3$-irregular if its vertices belong to pairwise distinct numbers of triangles. We prove that no $8$-regular $K_3$-irregular graph exists, settling the last unresolved case. Following the initial discovery of such graphs for regularities $r \in \{10,11,12\}$ (Stevanovi'c et al., 2024), our previous work (Hak et al., 2025) showed that no such graphs exist for $r \le 7$, provided the first example for $r=9$, and proved that any $8$-regular candidate must have between $17$ and $22$ vertices. We exclude these possible orders for $r=8$ by combining careful analysis of triangle degrees with integer linear programming techniques. Meanwhile, a recent construction (Zhang, 2026) established that regular $K_3$-irregular graphs do exist for all $r \ge 9$. Together with our results, this establishes that an $r$-regular $K_3$-irregular graph exists if and only if $r\geq 9$.
item.dc:creator: Artem Hak, Sergiy Kozerenko, Andrii Serdiuk

item.title: Symmetric, rational and infinitely many $(23_4)$ configurations, and the end of the existence problem for geometric $(n_4)$ configurations
item.description: arXiv:2610.14099v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A geometric $(n_4)$ configuration is a set of $n$ points and $n$ lines in the real projective plane such that every point lies on exactly four of the lines and every line contains exactly four of the points. The question of which $n$ admit such a configuration was posed by Gr\"unbaum in 2000, and successive work of Bokowski, Gr\"unbaum, Schewe, Pilaud and Cuntz settled every case but $n=23$. We settle this last case by bounding the symmetry of such configurations and classifying the most symmetric ones exactly. We prove that for every prime $n\equiv3\pmod4$ the group of projective symmetries of a geometric $(n_4)$ configuration has order at most four, explaining why symmetric constructions failed at $n=23$, and the same argument bounds the symmetry of $(n_5)$ configurations for primes $n\not\equiv1\pmod5$. Reducing the Klein four-group case to 4021 bilinear polynomial systems and solving all of them exactly with Gr\"obner bases, we show that exactly two $(23_4)$ configurations reach this bound up to projective equivalence and that there are no others even over $\mathbb{C}$. Both are self-polar; the first has integer coordinates and the second is defined over $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{17})$ but not over $\mathbb{Q}$. Consequently geometric $(n_4)$ configurations exist if and only if $n\ge18$ and $n\ne19$. The same classification recovers Cuntz's $(22_4)$ and $(26_4)$ configurations and finds three new combinatorial types at $n=22$ and $94$ at $n=26$. Among self-polar $(23_4)$ configurations with a single involution we find $50$ more, defined over number fields of degree at most $7$. Four of them deform in one-parameter families, and computing three of these exactly, one birational to the modular curve $X_1(11)$, we prove that there are infinitely many geometric $(23_4)$ configurations, among them infinitely many with rational coordinates that are self-polar and have no projective symmetry.
item.dc:creator: Wenhao Lu
